title: I Let the Youth Theater Cast List Policy Hit the Chair's Nephew

parts.text: I posted the callback list at 8:02 p.m. per the policy the chair wrote: scores, not surnames. The chair's nephew was not in the top twelve. She asked me to pencil him as ensemble extra with a solo. I was forty-two, volunteer MD, holding pencil 2B and a rubric. Extra with a solo is a lead. I photographed the rubric and her text. Then I posted the policy again on the parent Facebook she administered. At 8:14 she commented that community theater is about kindness, on a post that still had her score-not-surname graphic.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Her kindness comment is sitting under her own score graphic.

social.video_title: Ensemble extra with a solo was the nephew — Part 1/2
social.description: Callback twelve, 2B pencil, chair text. Facebook had her graphic. Would you have penciled him?

parts.text: The board kept the twelve. The nephew joined crew, which is a real job. Kindness handed him a headset. I music-directed people who had scores. The graphic stayed. She stayed admin and quieter. Community theater is about cues. Cues are not nephews. Opening night smelled like hairspray and fairness, which is a rare mix. I kept the 2B.

social.video_title: Crew headset is still a cue — Part 2/2
social.description: Top twelve held, nephew on crew, hairspray night. Was a solo a pencil?
